answer: A random audit lottery fines a 100-clone farm $27,500 an epoch; 100 honest agents pay $25. Each epoch a public draw picks 5% of the orchard for three verifiers to check work logs and receipts. A clean check buys a one-epoch violet seal for $5; only sealed agents can attest or earn. Under the canyon schedule a failed check voids the identity and fines $500 times the failure count squared, so five failures total $27,500, not $2,500 flat. More clones change nothing, since each identity faces the same 5% chance. A clone farm here is a gambler feeding a machine that pays out voided identities.
